newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steady, refinery runs supportive.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steady, refinery runs supportive.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices were steady on Tuesday despite softer futures as fresh refinery run cuts buoyed prices, especially for n+a material, traders and brokers said.

Shell cut crude throughput at its 350,000 barrels per day (bpd) Pernis refinery in Rotterdam by some 14 percent from Monday, trade sources said. This followed last week's cuts at Texaco and BP's Nerefco compex.
Pipeline quality material was talked at around June swaps levels of $192/$193 cif NWE, while n+a, and light naphtha with a minimum of 80 paraffins, were each pegged around $2 higher.

"A lot of the naphthas are still there, from North Africa and the like," one broker said, adding that reforming margins in Europe were currently "quite reasonable" and demand was good for the heavier grades as reforming feedstock.
Dealers suggested refining margins were artificially low in the short term partly because of the trading strategy of one player in the Brent crude market.
They pointed to the the market in Brent Contracts for Differences (cfds) - this week's cfds currently stand nearly 25 cents in backwardation to next week, with the following weeks flat to that.
